eventMetadata.context_description: Learner Tien enters the US Open round of 16 as the clear market favorite against Karen Khachanov, reflecting his stronger recent hard-court form and home-crowd support at Flushing Meadows. The 20-year-old American left-hander, ranked No. 15, has advanced with straight-set wins over Nuno Borges and Gael Monfils before outlasting Jakub Mensik in a five-set marathon, showing improved break-point conversion and second-serve resilience. Khachanov, the No. 50-ranked Russian veteran, has produced his best Grand Slam run of the year by upsetting third seed Felix Auger-Aliassime and posting straight-set victories over lower-ranked opponents, leveraging his 6-foot-6 frame and prior US Open semifinal experience. With no prior head-to-head matches, the contest highlights Tien’s current momentum and athletic edge against Khachanov’s proven big-stage resilience on outdoor hard courts.

title: Fed Decision in September?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's September 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for September 15-16, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their September meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent strong U.S. employment gains, including August nonfarm payrolls rising 162,000 and unemployment holding at 4.1%, have supported trader consensus for a 25 basis point federal funds rate increase at the mid-September FOMC meeting, while persistent core PCE inflation near 3.3% year-over-year and lingering energy price pressures from prior supply disruptions keep a hold outcome competitive. Hawkish signals from Chair Kevin Warsh and July dissents have reinforced expectations for tighter policy, yet recent monthly disinflation readings and uncertainty over August CPI data due before the meeting maintain the narrow gap. Incoming inflation prints, labor market revisions, or further Fed commentary could shift probabilities by clarifying whether demand pressures warrant immediate tightening or allow patience.

If the match is postponed or suspended, this market will remain open until the match has been completed. A postponement alone will not trigger a 50-50 resolution.
If a player retires, withdraws, is defaulted, or is disqualified, or the match otherwise begins but is not completed, this market will resolve based on any outcome that was already unequivocally determined at the time play stopped. An outcome is considered determined if it would have been guaranteed had the match been played to completion using the minimum number of additional sets required. For example, for a line of 2.5, if play stops with the players at one set each, completing the match would have required at least one additional set, resulting in at least 3 sets played, so "Over" would resolve as the winning outcome. If neither outcome was already determined at the time play stopped, this market will resolve 50-50.
If the match is canceled, or has not been completed by September 21, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve 50-50, unless an outcome was already unequivocally determined as described above.

eventMetadata.context_description: Arthur Gea, the 21-year-old Frenchman ranked No. 87 and a lucky loser, enters this US Open round-of-16 matchup on hard courts after a rapid rise that includes his first ATP title in Los Cabos and nine wins in his last ten matches. He has advanced through three rounds with five-set victories over Michael Zheng and others, showcasing improved hard-court form. Botic van de Zandschulp, ranked No. 70, brings veteran experience and recent momentum from upsets of Alex de Minaur and Zizou Bergs en route to the fourth round, plus prior wins over top-10 players this summer. Their limited prior encounters favor Gea from club play, though the Dutch player’s serve and return consistency on faster surfaces could prove decisive in what traders view as a competitive contest.

eventMetadata.context_description: Alexander Zverev enters the US Open round of 16 as the No. 2 seed and world No. 2 with a 49-13 season record, fresh off a French Open title and Wimbledon final. He has navigated early hard-court tests in New York, including five-set wins, while maintaining strong serving and baseline consistency. Luciano Darderi, ranked No. 22, reached this stage for the second Slam this year after straight-sets wins over lower-ranked opponents, but his lone prior victory over Zverev came on clay in Rome earlier in 2026. Their head-to-head is split 1-1, with no prior hard-court meetings, and Zverev’s experience, height advantage, and serve edge on outdoor hard courts shape the matchup. Darderi will need to replicate his return pressure and tiebreak resilience to challenge the favorite.

title: Israel closes its airspace by...?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Israel initiates a major closure of its airspace by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”. 

A “major closure” is defined as a broad closure, cancellation, or complete suspension of commercial aviation across the entirety of Israeli civilian airspace or a region encompassing a majority of Israeli civilian airspace, including commercial flights transiting, arriving in, and departing from that airspace. A qualifying closure must apply generally to all flights across Israel or a qualifying subset of Israeli airspace. Limited cancellations, delays, temporary ground stops or isolated regional closures will not qualify. Limited exceptions to a broad closure, however, will not disqualify such a closure from counting (e.g. exceptions for certain pre-approved flights may be permitted).

Warnings, No-Fly-Zones, flight suspensions, or other flight restrictions imposed by airlines or countries other than Israel will not be sufficient for a “Yes” resolution.

Airspace closures which occur solely due to weather conditions will not qualify.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Israeli aviation authorities; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

The Reds enter with momentum after winning seven of their last ten, while the Dodgers chase the NL's top seed amid roster depth concerns.

title: LoL: Invictus Gaming vs LGD Gaming (BO5) - LPL Playoffs
description:
This market refers to the LoL Lower bracket semifinal match between Invictus Gaming and LGD Gaming in the LPL Playoffs, initially scheduled for September 8, 2026 at 5:00 AM ET.

This market will resolve to "Invictus Gaming" if Invictus Gaming win the match against LGD Gaming.

This market will resolve to "LGD Gaming" if LGD Gaming win the match against Invictus Gaming.

If the match is canceled (not played at all) or ends in a tie, this market will resolve to 50-50.

If the match is postponed, it must be rescheduled to a start time on or before September 22, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET (14 calendar days after the originally scheduled start of September 8, 2026 at 5:00 AM ET). If, by that deadline, the most recently announced rescheduled start time is on or before the deadline, this market resolves based on the result of the match as played. Otherwise, this market resolves 50-50, regardless of whether the match is subsequently played.

If the match begins but is not completed, and one team wins due to the opponent's forfeiture, disqualification, or walkover, this market will resolve to the team who wins. 

If the match ends in a forfeit, disqualification, or walkover (team withdraws before the start and the other wins automatically), this market will resolve to 50-50. 

The resolution source for this market will be official information from https://gol.gg/esports/home. However, if https://gol.gg/esports/home has not published final results within 2 hours after the event’s conclusion, a consensus of credible reporting may be used instead including video evidence.

eventMetadata.context_description: Invictus Gaming enters the LPL lower-bracket semifinal as the trader favorite at roughly 64% implied probability, driven by recent BO5 resilience after sweeping through Top Esports 3-2 and Team WE 3-1 following a historic Nirvana-group run. TheShy’s aggressive top-lane pressure, Rookie’s consistent mid output, and Meiko’s shot-calling anchor a roster with proven group-fight execution. LGD Gaming counters with dark-horse momentum, having upset TES and Ninjas in Pyjamas in extended series behind Tangyuan’s mid-lane peaks, Shaoye’s decisive-game ADC carry, and Crisp’s vision control. The winner advances toward bubble-match positioning while the loser faces immediate elimination, with LGD’s long-series experience testing IG’s coordination under playoff pressure.

title: UEFA Champions League: 2027 Champion
description:
This market will resolve according to the team that wins the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League Championship.

If at any point it becomes impossible for a listed team to win the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League Championship per the rules of UEFA Champions League (e.g., they are eliminated in the playoffs), the corresponding market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source will be official information from UEFA Champions League; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: The 2026/27 UEFA Champions League title race remains tightly bunched among elite clubs because PSG enter as back-to-back champions yet face a deep field featuring Arsenal, Bayern Munich, Barcelona, Real Madrid, and Manchester City, each with proven depth and recent knockout experience. The league phase opening in September highlights balanced schedules and squad reinforcements across the Premier League, La Liga, and Bundesliga, where form, injury resilience, and home/away splits will shape advancement. Trader consensus reflects this parity, with no side exceeding low-20s implied probability amid strong historical records for these contenders in multi-leg ties and the expanded format. Late-season momentum shifts or key absences could still reorder the probabilities before the June 2027 final.
